title: TypeScript SDK: watch-mode typegen + annotated transformer for streaming discriminators and Zod/JSON-schema validators
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Add a developer-friendly incremental "watch" mode for the TypeScript SDK type generator that emits both declaration (.d.ts) files and small runtime validator artifacts. The generator will output annotated transformer helpers for common streaming patterns and discriminated-union resolution strategies, and provide an interoperable Zod and JSON-schema fallback so downstream services can validate structured LLM outputs with minimal overhead.
technical_design: Watchgen will run as a file-watching CLI for monorepo packages using a fast change index (mtime + file hash). For each changed prompt spec or shape file it will: 1) produce a minimal .d.ts for static typing, 2) emit a tiny runtime validator (zod schema + fast assertion helper) that can be imported at runtime, and 3) optionally emit a JSON-schema artifact for infra services. Discriminated unions are resolved via a two-pass strategy: primary tag-based discriminator (configurable tag name), then a lightweight shape-hint matcher generated from required property fingerprints. Streaming helpers include progressive validators that validate by chunk (prefix-safe), return partial typed values, and install safe fallbacks when shape confidence is below threshold. Artifacts are source-mapped back to the original schema files so editors and stack traces remain helpful.
implementation_steps: Add incremental file index and cache layer for monorepo package boundaries
Implement emitter pipeline: parse schema -> synthesize d.ts -> synthesize Zod runtime validators -> optional JSON-schema translator
Add progressive streaming validator API that exposes validateChunk(chunk) -> {status, partialValue, confidence}
Expose transformer helpers: mapStreamingTokensToObject, attachKVPrefixCacheHints, safeFallbackHandler
Wire up source maps to generator outputs for editor integration
Add unit tests for union resolution, streaming partial validation, and emitter correctness
Create docs and examples (chat streaming + file transform example) and migration guide
Rollout as experimental behind feature flag and collect usage metrics
acceptance_criteria: watchgen CLI runs and updates artifacts within <200ms for single-file edits in dev environment
Generated .d.ts files typecheck in a consumer package with no manual edits
Runtime Zod validators import with tree-shaking-friendly output and total added bundle <6KB gzipped per schema on average
Progressive streaming validator can produce a typed partial value for a 1-token increment and detect low-confidence shapes to trigger fallback policies
JSON-schema artifacts round-trip with Zod translator for at least 90% of our curated shape patterns
Source maps allow jumping from runtime validator back to schema file in VS Code
test_plan: Unit tests for emitter outputs (d.ts + zod + jsonschema), fuzz tests for union resolution heuristics, integration test that runs an end-to-end chat streaming example validating partial outputs, and performance test measuring watch latency and emitted artifact sizes. Tests will run in CI with a lightweight synthetic repo and a larger monorepo fixture.
rollout_plan: Stage 1: feature branch + opt-in release to internal dev team. Stage 2: experimental flag in ts-sdk 1.8 release with docs and example app. Stage 3: monitor errors and bundle impact for 2 weeks, gather feedback. Stage 4: enable by default in 1.9 if no regressions and after minor perf tuning.
notes: Goal is to reduce friction for engineers building streaming-first integrations and keep runtime validation small and opt-in.
Consider aligning JSON-schema output with existing console ingestion contracts to make policy checks easier.
We should measure typical schema complexity across customers to optimize default emitter compression and zod-lite usage.
